# <span id="aanchor21"></span> Liquid Quality Source Editor

[&lt;&lt; Back](Liquid%20Quality%20Source%20Editor.md#Menus) \| [File](File%20Menu.md) \| <a href="#" class="selected">Validations</a> \| [Tools](Tools%20Menu.md)

## Validations Menu

Validations will be run automatically on imports and edits when validations are enabled. Each validation tab is enabled individually by checking the option to Enable. Enabled validations can also be run manually from the **Review** \> **Run Validations** menu.

All exceptions generated can be viewed from the Exception Resolver.

This feature requires the **Source Analysis** module.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 568;height: 347;" />

The Show History button allows users to view the history of validation set points across all tabs. This includes what changes, who made the change, and when. The button is available when the Log Validation Set Point History option is checked within FLOWCAL Configuration.

The following tabs are available in the Validations menu:

- **Min/Max** - Min/Max performs a comparison of all the minimum and maximum values for each of the components. If Enable Min/Max is checked, the values entered for all the analysis components will be validated during import and if the value is out of range then an exception will be generated.

  <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Mol Pct Normalization">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Mol % Normalization</a>

  <div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Mol Pct Normalization">

  Source Analysis can be enabled to normalize imported samples if the total mole percent is not 100% but is within a minimum and maximum value.

  The following options are available for Mole % Normalization:

  - **System** – When selected in the Source Editor, FLOWCAL will use the System Configuration limits for Mole % Normalization. This will enable the user to manage limits for all sources.
  - **Source Quality** – When selected, the local source limits are used. This will enable the user to place custom normalization per source.
  - **No Normalization** – When selected, normalization will not occur for any source. Exceptions will not be written if this option is enabled.

  If the analysis total is outside the normalization range, the analysis will NOT be normalized. Only analysis totals within the range will be normalized. If the normalization does not occur, [exception 3719 or 3720](../../Exceptions/Exception%20Directory/3000/3700-3799.md) will be written.

  The Mole % Normalization Minimum and Maximum values shown in the Quality tab for Source Validations are read only. These values are configuration within System Configuration or the Liquid Quality Source.

  </div>

- **Radical Change** - Radical Change is a comparison of the current analysis to the previous analysis based on percent or unit difference. If the Enabled Radical Change is checked, the values entered for all the analysis components will be validated during import. If the difference between the current analysis and the previous analysis exceeds the limit set, then an exception will be generated.

- **Frozen Value** - Frozen Value performs a comparison of selected parameters to prior records to recognize an interruption in a live data feed. This filter is user configurable as to the number of repeated records and which parameters to consider, as well as a limit. This is especially useful with online chromatograph data to identify if a liquid chromatograph was left in calibration mode or if SCADA is not being updated with new values.

- **Expert System** - Expert System employs statistical analysis to perform historical data review to identify uncharacteristic changes in liquid quality source data. This function provides the user with numerous configurable set points that allow the user to customize a validation to each individual liquid quality source. The data is validated to make sure a given data point is within a user-defined number of standard deviations from the prior set of samples.

- **Variance** - Variance validations compare the GPMs provided by the lab against the GPMs that FLOWCAL calculates. If the difference is outside the limits established, then an exception will be generated.

</div>
